name: Metro Map
author: István Koren
description: Renders an object-centric process as a transit-schematic 'metro map': activities become stations shared across object types, object types become color-coded lines routed with 45°-only turns and consistent parallel lane order, top to bottom in roughly process time order. Discover it from an Object-Centric Petri Net (choice/parallelism drawn as X/+ gateways read off the net structure) or from an Object-Centric Directly-Follows Graph (no gateways, but real per-station/per-arc frequencies and a complexity slider). Both mine their upstream model transparently as an internal stage.

objectTypes.title: Object types
objectTypes.description: Which object types participate in discovery. Empty means every object type present in the log.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT object_type AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {object} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

minerVariant.title: Miner variant
minerVariant.description: IM guarantees every object type's lifecycle replays every trace it was discovered from. IMf gives that up in exchange for ignoring infrequent behavior, and is the usual choice on a real log. Forwarded to run.promenade.ocpn's own discovery, run internally.

noiseThreshold.title: Noise threshold
noiseThreshold.description: IMf only. How weak a path has to be, relative to the strongest alternative, before it is treated as noise. Applied independently within each object type's own lifecycle.

maxObjectTypes.title: Object type limit
maxObjectTypes.description: Discovery keeps only the most frequent object types, up to this many. Forwarded to core.discover.ocdfg, run internally. Hide individual types afterwards from the view's own legend.

rankTiebreak.title: Rank tie-break
rankTiebreak.description: Ranking (which row a station lands on, top to bottom) needs the whole model to be acyclic, but two object types can each flow acyclically through their own lifecycle and still form a cycle only once merged, purely from sharing stations — something has to give. "Frequency" (default) always keeps the busier direction and discounts the rarer one, so a rare cross-type wraparound can no longer outrank a station's own high-traffic through-line. "Structural" instead breaks that tie the way every diagram used to: fast and deterministic, but which of the two directions it keeps is an accident of station name order, unrelated to which one is actually the real flow.

stationStyle.title: Stations
stationStyle.description: Draw activities as Budapest-metro interchange dots (with the name beside them) or as labeled rectangles.

edgeLabel.title: Edge labels
edgeLabel.description: What to print on each arc. "Frequency" is the observed count; "Performance" is the mean wait between the two activities. Only shown for a map discovered from an OC-DFG — a Petri net is a structural model whose arcs carry no counts or timestamps. "Performance" needs core.discover.ocdfg 0.2.0 or later: re-discover any OC-DFG map made before that.

animateFlow.title: Animate flow
animateFlow.description: Send a traveling pulse along every line in its process direction (source to target). Purely decorative; off by default.

preserveStability.title: Preserve layout stability
preserveStability.description: On (default): moving the complexity slider only ever reveals more detail, never reshuffles what is already shown — the filtered view is a monotone refinement of the full model's own rank and lane. Off: every slider position is laid out fresh from only the currently visible stations and arcs, as if the hidden ones did not exist. Häge & Rehse, "Mental Maps in Process Mining: Does Stabilizing DFGs Improve Process Analysis Performance?" (BPM 2025), found no positive effect from stabilisation on process-analysis performance in their study.
